units: Picture a one-metre ruler. Would 75 cm reach its far end? Compare that with a cable seven and a half metres long.
One metre already contains 100 centimetres. When the counting unit gets bigger, should the same cable need more units or fewer?
scale: Write 10⁻³ and 10⁻⁵ as fractions with 1 on top. Which denominator makes the smaller piece?
The leading 2s match. What changes when the number of places in the denominator changes?
relationships: Imagine continuing for a second hour at the same speed. Does that extra hour add any distance?
In distance = speed × time, which input changed? Is time a multiplier or a divisor?
vectors: Draw the route to scale. Is the question asking for all the ground you covered or for the arrow from start to finish?
Mark your starting point before drawing the westward part. Where does that second arrow begin?
graphs: Read the unit beside the vertical axis. Does the height of this line show a place or a speed?
Choose two different times on the flat line. Do their positions give you any evidence of a changing speed?
accumulation: Try adding the change for each of the four seconds. Which operation does that repeat?
Which way does the minus sign in the velocity say the cart is moving? Carry that direction into your answer.
uncertainty: Imagine every reading is made with the same misplaced ruler mark. Would repeating the reading put that mark in a new place?
More digits describe a reading more finely. What would actually move the instrument’s zero to the right place?
models: Which speed range already gave predictions that agreed with measurements?
Measurements let you test a prediction. Which part can be revised without changing what was observed?
check-units: Write metres per second as m/s, then multiply by s. Which matching factors cancel?
Trace the length unit through (m/s) × s. What happens to the two time factors?
